helping micro small and medium enterprises msmes enhance their market reach promote their products and services and improve their competitiveness in domestic and international markets. under this scheme nsic provides support through participation in trade fairs exhibitions buyer-seller meets vendor development programs marketing events e-marketing platforms and business networking opportunities. the scheme is designed to address the marketing challenges faced by msmes and enable them to connect with potential buyers government agencies large corporations and export markets. it is primarily used by manufacturing and service-sector msmes startups entrepreneurs women-led enterprises artisan groups cooperatives and small businesses seeking to expand their customer base and increase sales. the major advantages of the scheme include enhanced market visibility increased business opportunities access to new customers participation in national and international exhibitions improved brand recognition opportunities for business networking support for market expansion and greater exposure to procurement opportunities from government and private sector buyers. common grievances related to the scheme may include delays in approval for participation in exhibitions or trade fairs non-receipt of marketing assistance delays in reimbursement of eligible expenses lack of communication regarding marketing events difficulties in accessing e-marketing platforms exclusion from buyer-seller meets despite eligibility issues related to registration for promotional activities or delays in processing applications under the scheme. for example an msme may complain that its application to participate in an nsic-sponsored trade exhibition has been pending for an extended information about buyer-seller meets and vendor development programs for which it had registered. overall the marketing facilitation scheme aims to strengthen the marketing capabilities of msmes by providing platforms for product promotion business networking buyer engagement and market expansion thereby supporting enterprise growth improving sales opportunities enhancing competitiveness and contributing to the long-term development of the msme sector.

Others. Media, Vigilance. media and vigilance in msme together ensure transparency accountability and public trust in the functioning of the ministry of micro small and medium enterprises. the media function focuses on communicating government policies schemes achievements and events through official press releases social media updates and coordination with national and regional media so that msme entrepreneurs and the general public remain informed about opportunities milestones alerts and policy changes. effective media outreach improves scheme visibility encourages participation and builds confidence by presenting accurate and timely information. in parallel the vigilance function safeguards integrity within msme offices development institutes and technology centres by preventing corruption conducting inspections and internal audits examining complaints coordinating investigations where required promoting vigilance awareness and ensuring compliance with rules and procedures. vigilance mechanisms also support transparency through lawful disclosures and accountability processes thereby protecting public funds and maintaining ethical standards in scheme implementation and administration. examples of grievances related to media and vigilance include delay or omission of important msme events or scheme launches in official press releases inaccurate or incomplete media reporting leading to confusion among entrepreneurs lack of coverage of regional or hindi-language initiatives unresponsiveness to media or public information requests prolonged delay in vigilance investigations despite prescribed timelines inaction on corruption or misconduct complaints denial of information related to vigilance matters without clear justification and inadequate participation or seriousness in vigilance awareness or inspection programs.

UAM/Udyam Registration/Certificate related issues. Updation of Address Details. this category refers to grievances related to updating or correcting the registered address of an enterprise in the udyam registration records. the registered address represents the official location of the enterprise and accurate address information is important for maintaining correct business records and identifying the location of operations. grievances under this category commonly occur when the enterprise has changed its business location after registration or when the address recorded during registration was entered incorrectly. entrepreneurs may request an update if the business has shifted to a new office factory or operational location. some grievances arise when the address contains typographical errors incomplete information or mismatched details that do not correspond with supporting documents. in other cases users may report that they are unable to modify the address details through the portal or that the changes they submitted have not been updated in the registration record. these grievances are usually raised by msme owners proprietors partners of partnership firms directors of companies or authorized representatives responsible for maintaining enterprise records. small business owners who relocate their operations to a different city or premises may request updates to ensure the registration reflects the correct address. similarly compliance officers accountants or consultants managing regulatory documentation for the enterprise may submit grievances when they identify discrepancies between the registered address and the actual business location.

International Trade Fair (ITF). this category covers the international trade fair itf scheme which refers to initiatives that support the participation of micro small and medium enterprises msmes in international trade fairs exhibitions expos buyer-seller meets and other global marketing events. the scheme aims to help msmes showcase their products and services in international markets establish business relationships with overseas buyers explore export opportunities and enhance their global competitiveness. it is primarily used by msme manufacturers exporters startups entrepreneurs artisan groups cooperatives women-led enterprises and service providers seeking to expand their presence in foreign markets. the major advantages of the scheme include increased international market exposure access to potential buyers and distributors opportunities for export promotion business networking brand visibility market intelligence product promotion and support for global business expansion. common grievances under this category may include delays in approval of applications for participation in trade fairs non-receipt of financial assistance or reimbursement delays in processing travel or exhibition-related support lack of communication regarding event schedules or participation status issues in beneficiary selection difficulties in obtaining participation certificates inadequate support during international events and delays in settlement of eligible claims. for example an msme exporter may complain that approval for participation in an international trade fair has not been received despite timely submission of the application a beneficiary may report that reimbursement for exhibition expenses remains pending after completion of the event an entrepreneur may seek clarification regarding rejection of their application for participation a business owner may raise concerns about not receiving information related to exhibition logistics or event arrangements or a participant may report difficulties in obtaining post-event support or documentation promised under the scheme. overall this category serves as a platform for addressing grievances related to international trade fair participation and associated support mechanisms helping msmes access global markets strengthen export capabilities enhance international business opportunities and contribute to the growth of india s export-oriented enterprise ecosystem.

Loans and Credit Support. Finance Related. finance-related schemes for msmes comprise a comprehensive set of credit subsidy and guarantee initiatives implemented by the government of india through the ministry of micro small and medium enterprises and allied institutions such as the small industries development bank of india to improve formal financial access for micro small and medium enterprises. these schemes include the credit guarantee fund trust for micro and small enterprises cgtmse for collateral-free loans with partial guarantee coverage pradhan mantri mudra yojana pmmy for micro-credit to small units prime minister s employment generation programme pmegp providing margin money subsidies for new ventures emergency credit line guarantee scheme eclgs for liquidity support to stressed msmes credit linked capital subsidy scheme clcss for technology upgradation stand-up india for women and sc st entrepreneurs interest subvention schemes to reduce borrowing costs and financing and raw material assistance programs of national small industries corporation. collectively these schemes promote collateral-free and affordable credit reduce financial risk through guarantees and subsidies encourage technology adoption and productivity gains provide emergency liquidity during downturns and support entrepreneurship employment generation and inclusive growth across the msme sector. however msmes often encounter operational challenges in availing these benefits. examples of grievances include banks demanding collateral despite enterprises being eligible for cgtmse-backed loans delays in release of pmegp margin money subsidies due to verification or procedural backlogs denial of interest subvention benefits because of data mismatches or missing udyam registration linkage exclusion of otherwise eligible units from emergency credit facilities on subjective risk grounds by lending institutions and rejection of technology upgradation subsidy claims under clcss due to machinery or documentation disputes all of which are commonly escalated through banking grievance channels or msme grievance redressal mechanisms.

MSME Policy/Industry Associations related issues. msme policy industry associations related issues refer to the institutional support framework under india s msme ecosystem in which industry associations both geographic and sectoral aggregate msmes to represent their interests advocate for policy reforms and facilitate implementation of government schemes. associations such as federation of indian chambers of commerce and industry and confederation of indian industry act as collective voices for msmes engaging with governments on issues like access to credit public procurement delayed payments and regulatory simplification. they also deliver shared services including skill development technology upgradation market access support and information dissemination and often function as implementing or partner agencies for msme schemes through coordination with development commissioner msme . while this collective model strengthens bargaining power improves outreach of schemes and promotes responsible and sustainable business practices associations frequently face structural constraints such as limited financial resources inadequate technical expertise and uneven advocacy capacity which affect their effectiveness. common grievances raised through these associations include policy demands being ignored or inadequately addressed for example exclusion of msme-specific relief measures during economic packages weak enforcement of delayed payment mechanisms despite persistent follow-up by associations slow or uneven implementation of government schemes at the state level and insufficient support for labor- and compliance-related challenges. examples of grievances include petitions by bodies like the tamil nadu small industries association seeking relief measures such as wage support or one-time settlements during economic disruptions that did not translate into policy action repeated representations regarding the ineffectiveness of delayed payment resolution mechanisms where enforcement remains weak resource shortages within associations that limit their ability to offer fee-based training advisory or national-level advocacy demands for intervention when layoffs or financial stress among large buyers adversely impact msme suppliers and cases where state-level grievance redressal cells fail to resolve regulatory or operational issues promptly forcing associations to escalate matters to higher authorities.

DBT / IT desk including Annual Report. dbt it desk including the annual report in msme refers to the data dbt wing functioning under the office of the development commissioner msme which is responsible for administering direct benefit transfer dbt of subsidies under msme schemes managing it and digital infrastructure and compiling the ministry s annual report. the wing oversees end-to-end dbt processes for scheme reimbursements such as ict and cloud computing subsidies where msmes initially incur eligible expenses and subsequently receive reimbursements directly into aadhaar-linked bank accounts through the public financial management system often after technical verification by agencies like telecommunications consultants india limited. it ensures compliance with national dbt standards in coordination with the dbt mission and national informatics centre maintains and upgrades msme it systems including the udyam registration portal supports cloud-based it adoption for msmes undertakes data analytics and mis reporting and onboards schemes to the national dbt framework. the wing also prepares the annual report of the ministry of msme consolidating performance indicators financial outlays scheme outcomes udyam registration trends and macro-level contributions such as msme share in gdp and employment which are used for parliament cabinet briefings and policy evaluation. while this framework promotes transparency leak-proof subsidy delivery evidence-based policymaking and digital efficiency stakeholders frequently raise grievances related to dbt execution data accuracy it reliability and reporting quality. examples of grievances include msmes experiencing delays in receipt of approved ict or cloud service subsidies due to pfms transaction or verification glitches reimbursement failures arising from aadhaar bank account linkage mismatches despite valid udyam registration inaccuracies or under-reporting of scheme achievements udyam registrations or msme gdp contribution in the annual report affecting policy advocacy and planning temporary downtime or access issues on udyam or other msme it portals during registration or subsidy claim periods and gaps in mis capture where scheme data duplications or leakages are not properly reflected in dbt dashboards or the annual report prompting appeals for correction and system strengthening.

sentences: Others. Official Language Related Issues. official language related issues in msme administration concern the implementation of hindi rajbhasha in accordance with the official languages act <NUM> as amended across the ministry of msme its development institutes field offices and attached organizations. this framework mandates progressive use of hindi in official work bilingual hindi english documentation replies in hindi to communications received in hindi availability of hindi-enabled software on computers and regular training in hindi typing and computing for officials. the ministry monitors compliance through official language implementation committees quarterly progress reviews rajbhasha inspections and conferences while ensuring that citizens charters schemes portals and public-facing information are available bilingually. these measures aim to improve accessibility for hindi-speaking msmes enhance transparency and inclusiveness strengthen regional outreach especially in hindi-belt states and fulfill constitutional and administrative obligations without restricting the use of english where required. examples of grievances include non-hindi reply an msme submits an application or grievance in hindi to a development institute but receives a response only in english contrary to official language correspondence rules. bilingual documentation gap key documents such as annual reports scheme guidelines or notices are issued only in english or with incomplete hindi translations limiting accessibility for hindi-speaking stakeholders. training shortfall field office staff are unable to type or process files in hindi despite mandated hindi software and training provisions causing delays in rajbhasha compliance. portal language issue hindi versions of portals like udyam or champions contain missing pages partial translations or technical glitches preventing rural or hindi-only users from completing registrations or filing grievances. awareness and communication lapse regional msmes are not informed in hindi about official language conferences workshops or policy updates leading to missed participation and reduced stakeholder engagement.

Others. Media, Vigilance. media and vigilance in msme together ensure transparency accountability and public trust in the functioning of the ministry of micro small and medium enterprises. the media function focuses on communicating government policies schemes achievements and events through official press releases social media updates and coordination with national and regional media so that msme entrepreneurs and the general public remain informed about opportunities milestones alerts and policy changes. effective media outreach improves scheme visibility encourages participation and builds confidence by presenting accurate and timely information. in parallel the vigilance function safeguards integrity within msme offices development institutes and technology centres by preventing corruption conducting inspections and internal audits examining complaints coordinating investigations where required promoting vigilance awareness and ensuring compliance with rules and procedures. vigilance mechanisms also support transparency through lawful disclosures and accountability processes thereby protecting public funds and maintaining ethical standards in scheme implementation and administration. examples of grievances related to media and vigilance include delay or omission of important msme events or scheme launches in official press releases inaccurate or incomplete media reporting leading to confusion among entrepreneurs lack of coverage of regional or hindi-language initiatives unresponsiveness to media or public information requests prolonged delay in vigilance investigations despite prescribed timelines inaction on corruption or misconduct complaints denial of information related to vigilance matters without clear justification and inadequate participation or seriousness in vigilance awareness or inspection programs.

UAM/Udyam Registration/Certificate related issues. Updation of Address Details. this category refers to grievances related to updating or correcting the registered address of an enterprise in the udyam registration records. the registered address represents the official location of the enterprise and accurate address information is important for maintaining correct business records and identifying the location of operations. grievances under this category commonly occur when the enterprise has changed its business location after registration or when the address recorded during registration was entered incorrectly. entrepreneurs may request an update if the business has shifted to a new office factory or operational location. some grievances arise when the address contains typographical errors incomplete information or mismatched details that do not correspond with supporting documents. in other cases users may report that they are unable to modify the address details through the portal or that the changes they submitted have not been updated in the registration record. these grievances are usually raised by msme owners proprietors partners of partnership firms directors of companies or authorized representatives responsible for maintaining enterprise records. small business owners who relocate their operations to a different city or premises may request updates to ensure the registration reflects the correct address. similarly compliance officers accountants or consultants managing regulatory documentation for the enterprise may submit grievances when they identify discrepancies between the registered address and the actual business location.

sentences: Schemes and Programs . International Trade Fair (ITF). this category covers the international trade fair itf scheme which refers to initiatives that support the participation of micro small and medium enterprises msmes in international trade fairs exhibitions expos buyer-seller meets and other global marketing events. the scheme aims to help msmes showcase their products and services in international markets establish business relationships with overseas buyers explore export opportunities and enhance their global competitiveness. it is primarily used by msme manufacturers exporters startups entrepreneurs artisan groups cooperatives women-led enterprises and service providers seeking to expand their presence in foreign markets. the major advantages of the scheme include increased international market exposure access to potential buyers and distributors opportunities for export promotion business networking brand visibility market intelligence product promotion and support for global business expansion. common grievances under this category may include delays in approval of applications for participation in trade fairs non-receipt of financial assistance or reimbursement delays in processing travel or exhibition-related support lack of communication regarding event schedules or participation status issues in beneficiary selection difficulties in obtaining participation certificates inadequate support during international events and delays in settlement of eligible claims. for example an msme exporter may complain that approval for participation in an international trade fair has not been received despite timely submission of the application a beneficiary may report that reimbursement for exhibition expenses remains pending after completion of the event an entrepreneur may seek clarification regarding rejection of their application for participation a business owner may raise concerns about not receiving information related to exhibition logistics or event arrangements or a participant may report difficulties in obtaining post-event support or documentation promised under the scheme. overall this category serves as a platform for addressing grievances related to international trade fair participation and associated support mechanisms helping msmes access global markets strengthen export capabilities enhance international business opportunities and contribute to the growth of india s export-oriented enterprise ecosystem.

Loans and Credit Support. Finance Related. finance-related schemes for msmes comprise a comprehensive set of credit subsidy and guarantee initiatives implemented by the government of india through the ministry of micro small and medium enterprises and allied institutions such as the small industries development bank of india to improve formal financial access for micro small and medium enterprises. these schemes include the credit guarantee fund trust for micro and small enterprises cgtmse for collateral-free loans with partial guarantee coverage pradhan mantri mudra yojana pmmy for micro-credit to small units prime minister s employment generation programme pmegp providing margin money subsidies for new ventures emergency credit line guarantee scheme eclgs for liquidity support to stressed msmes credit linked capital subsidy scheme clcss for technology upgradation stand-up india for women and sc st entrepreneurs interest subvention schemes to reduce borrowing costs and financing and raw material assistance programs of national small industries corporation. collectively these schemes promote collateral-free and affordable credit reduce financial risk through guarantees and subsidies encourage technology adoption and productivity gains provide emergency liquidity during downturns and support entrepreneurship employment generation and inclusive growth across the msme sector. however msmes often encounter operational challenges in availing these benefits. examples of grievances include banks demanding collateral despite enterprises being eligible for cgtmse-backed loans delays in release of pmegp margin money subsidies due to verification or procedural backlogs denial of interest subvention benefits because of data mismatches or missing udyam registration linkage exclusion of otherwise eligible units from emergency credit facilities on subjective risk grounds by lending institutions and rejection of technology upgradation subsidy claims under clcss due to machinery or documentation disputes all of which are commonly escalated through banking grievance channels or msme grievance redressal mechanisms.

Schemes and Programs . Related to Scheme of KVIC - Khadi Vikas Yojana. this category has grievances related to khadi vikas yojana a kvic-led scheme under the ministry of msme that supports khadi artisans and institutions through market assistance concessional credit support workshed assistance infrastructure strengthening and marketing promotion. it covers issues that arise when beneficiaries apply for scheme benefits but face delays rejection incomplete support subsidy problems or implementation failures at the institutional district or bank level. this category is generally used by khadi artisans khadi institutions village industry units rural entrepreneurs self-help groups and other eligible beneficiaries who are involved in spinning weaving production marketing or institution development under the khadi ecosystem. the main problems solved in this category are improving artisans income strengthening khadi production infrastructure supporting easier access to credit and promoting marketing and sales of khadi products. common grievances can include delay in release of assistance non-availability of promised support rejection of subsidy or reimbursement claims inadequate workshed or infrastructure support and mismatch between approved and received benefits. five example grievances are a workshed assistance approval not being released on time delayed processing of concessional credit support marketing renovation work not starting after sanction subsidy claim rejection due to documentation issues and post-inspection follow-up stopping after approval.
